newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian insurers feud over oil company account.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian insurers feud over oil company account.

text.p: Six Nigerian firms launched a legal tussle on Monday over the lucrative insurance account of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
High court judge Mahmud Belgore fixed November 27 and 28 for hearing on the case to decide which of the six firms has right of control over the NNPC account, worth 2.025 billion naira.

Two of firms -- Fidelity Bond of Nigeria and Trinity Mills Insurance Brokers -- want the court to prevent oil minister Dan Etete from either taking the NNPC account from their control or transferring it to four others.
The four are: UNIC Insurance, Industrial and General Insurance Company Limited, Inter-Continental Insurance Company Limited and Kapital Insurance Company Nigeria Limited.
All six companies are 100 percent owned by Nigerians.
Lawyers for Fidelity Bond and Trinity Mills allege that Etete was using his official position to transfer the NNPC account to the other four firms.

"It is not competent for the Petroleum Resources Minister to appoint the four other insurance firms as insurers of the assets of the NNPC," they said in a sworn affidavit presented to the court on Monday.
State insurer NICON brokered the appointment of their clients, they said, adding that they were entitled to receive all commissions payable by NICON.
The lawyers alleged Etete notified NICON that military ruler General Sani Abacha had approved that the state insurer should no longer be responsible for insuring all government assets.
But they said an official statement released in February last year required all assets of government or its agencies to be insured with NICON.

"Our clients are legal insurers of the NNPC assets for this year as contained in the letter of November 28, 1995 inviting them to broker the NNPC assets and letter of May 2, 1996 by NNPC confirming and re-confirming the appointments," their affidavit said.
The other parties will state their own side when hearing resumes towards the end of this month.
The NNPC assets whose insurance is involved include oil refineries, oil depots and sundry other properties.
